strings.d1.s0.name: Charles Bridge
strings.d1.s0.tips: A 14th-century bridge lined with 30 statues. It is empty before 8 am. Touch the statue of John of Nepomuk.
strings.d1.s1.name: Old Town Square
strings.d1.s1.tips: Týn Church and the Jan Hus monument. The Astronomical Clock performs every hour from 09:00 to 23:00 (the 12 apostles).
strings.d1.s2.name: Old Town Hall Tower
strings.d1.s2.tips: A tower with a lift and panoramic views over the square. No queues in the morning.
strings.d1.s3.name: Jewish Quarter Josefov
strings.d1.s3.tips: Old-New Synagogue, Old Jewish Cemetery (12,000 gravestones) and the Pinkas Synagogue. Closed on Saturdays.
strings.d1.s4.name: Lokál Dlouhá
strings.d1.s4.tips: Beer from the best Pilsner Urquell tank, plus svíčková (beef in cream sauce) and goulash. A classic Czech canteen.
strings.d1.b0.name: Sisters Bistro
strings.d1.b1.name: Klementinum
strings.d1.b1.tips: Baroque library and astronomical tower. Swap for Josefov.
strings.d2.s0.name: Prague Castle
strings.d2.s0.tips: The world's largest castle complex: St Vitus Cathedral (Mucha stained glass), the Old Royal Palace and Golden Lane (Kafka's No. 22). Arrive at the 09:00 opening, book a timed ticket in summer, and expect security checks at the gate.
strings.d2.s1.name: Malá Strana Walk
strings.d2.s1.tips: Marked houses along Nerudova Street, and the baroque St Nicholas Church (dome).
strings.d2.s2.name: U Modré Kachničky
strings.d2.s2.tips: The Blue Duck: goose and duck are Bohemian classics. In Malá Strana.
strings.d2.s3.name: Kampa Island & Museum
strings.d2.s3.tips: A park on a river island with David Černý's babies and the Kampa Museum (Kupka), 350 CZK.
strings.d2.s4.name: Petřín Hill Funicular & Tower
strings.d2.s4.tips: The funicular takes a tram ticket. The 63 m mini Eiffel Tower has 299 steps. Go for sunset.
strings.d2.b0.name: Café Savoy
strings.d2.b0.tips: A café from 1893 with a painted ceiling, in Malá Strana.
strings.d2.b1.name: Strahov Monastery Library
strings.d2.b1.tips: Baroque library and beer. Swap for Petřín.
strings.d3.s0.name: Vyšehrad
strings.d3.s0.tips: A hilltop fortress that predates Prague Castle. See the Slavín cemetery (Dvořák, Mucha), the Rotunda and river views. Free.
strings.d3.s1.name: Vinohradský Parlament
strings.d3.s1.tips: A Czech restaurant in Vinohrady. Try vepřo knedlo zelo (pork, dumplings and cabbage).
strings.d3.s2.name: Riegrovy Sady
strings.d3.s2.tips: A park beer garden with views of the castle. Sunset in summer.
strings.d3.s3.name: Žižkov Television Tower
strings.d3.s3.tips: Černý's climbing babies and a 93 m observation deck.
strings.d3.s4.name: U Slovanské Lípy
strings.d3.s4.tips: An old Žižkov pub with more than 10 tank beers and pork knuckle.
strings.d3.b0.name: Kavárna Slavia
strings.d3.b0.tips: A riverside café from 1884, opposite the National Theatre.
strings.d3.b1.name: National Museum
strings.d3.b1.tips: At the top of Wenceslas Square, with a dome. Swap for Žižkov.
strings.d4.s0.name: Sedlec Ossuary
strings.d4.s0.tips: 1 hour by train (Hlavní). Chandeliers and a coat of arms made from 40,000 skeletons (the Bone Church). Buy tickets online. No photography.
strings.d4.s1.name: St. Barbara's Cathedral
strings.d4.s1.tips: The Gothic cathedral of the silver miners. UNESCO-listed, with a terrace at the Jesuit College.
strings.d4.s2.name: Kutná Hora Historic Centre
strings.d4.s2.tips: Medieval streets, the Stone Fountain and the Italian Court (the mint).
strings.d4.s3.name: Dačický Kutná Hora
strings.d4.s3.tips: A medieval beer hall serving local beer and duck.
strings.d4.s4.name: Czech Museum of Silver Hrádek
strings.d4.s4.tips: Descend into a medieval silver mine (helmet and apron provided). Guided tour, then the train back.
strings.d4.b0.name: Karlštejn Castle
strings.d4.b0.tips: Charles IV's Gothic castle, 40 minutes by train. Swap for Kutná Hora (closed Mondays).
strings.d4.b1.name: Pivnice Dačický Bahçe
strings.d4.b1.tips: The garden of the same venue. Sausages.
strings.d5.s0.name: Letná Park Metronome
strings.d5.s0.tips: A metronome stands where the Stalin statue once was. Views of the bridges and a beer garden (summer).
strings.d5.s1.name: National Technical Museum
strings.d5.s1.tips: Aeroplanes, trains and vintage cars, in Letná.
strings.d5.s2.name: Holešovice Market Hall
strings.d5.s2.tips: Pražská tržnice: Vietnamese pho and Czech food stalls.
strings.d5.s3.name: DOX Centre for Contemporary Art
strings.d5.s3.tips: Contemporary art and a rooftop airship, in Holešovice.
strings.d5.s4.name: Stromovka Park
strings.d5.s4.tips: A former royal hunting park with ponds and a planetarium.
strings.d5.b0.name: Prague Zoo
strings.d5.b0.tips: One of Europe's best zoos (Troja). Swap for DOX and Stromovka.
strings.d5.b1.name: Bistro 8 Letná
strings.d6.s0.name: Český Krumlov Castle
strings.d6.s0.tips: RegioJet bus, 3 hours (Florenc, about 200 CZK, leave at 07:00). A UNESCO town in a bend of the Vltava with the country's second-largest castle. Tower 180 CZK, baroque theatre tour.
strings.d6.s1.name: Castle Garden Český Krumlov
strings.d6.s1.tips: Cascading gardens and a revolving auditorium theatre.
strings.d6.s2.name: Krčma v Šatlavské
strings.d6.s2.tips: A medieval dungeon tavern serving meat cooked over an open fire.
strings.d6.s3.name: Český Krumlov Old Town
strings.d6.s3.tips: Latrán and the square, plus the Egon Schiele Art Centrum (200 CZK).
strings.d6.s4.name: Vltava Rafting Krumlov
strings.d6.s4.tips: A 1-hour rubber boat ride through the town. The weirs are fun (May to September).
strings.d6.b0.name: Papa's Living Restaurant Krumlov
strings.d6.b1.name: Hluboká Castle
strings.d6.b1.tips: A white, Windsor-style castle. An alternative on the way to Krumlov.
strings.d7.s0.name: Wenceslas Square
strings.d7.s0.tips: The square of the 1989 Velvet Revolution. The National Museum stands at the top, and the upside-down horse hangs in Lucerna Passage.
strings.d7.s1.name: Havelské Tržiště
strings.d7.s1.tips: A market in the Old Town for souvenirs and fruit. Try Moser for Bohemian crystal.
strings.d7.s2.name: Café Louvre
strings.d7.s2.tips: A café from 1902 (Kafka, Einstein). Farewell breakfast and billiards.
strings.d7.s3.name: Hlavní Nádraží Airport Bus
strings.d7.s3.tips: The AE bus takes 35 minutes, or take the metro plus bus 119. Farewell.
strings.d7.b0.name: Trdelník Stand Old Town
strings.d7.b0.tips: Trdelník with ice cream (touristy but tasty). A farewell treat.
strings.d7.b1.name: Mucha Museum
strings.d7.b1.tips: Art nouveau posters. Swap for the market.
strings.note0: A Lítačka 24-hour ticket costs 120 CZK (tram, metro and funicular). The centre is walkable. The AE bus to the airport costs 100 CZK. Use Bolt or Uber instead of taxis.
strings.note1: Summers are 25-30°C. Visit Charles Bridge before 7:30, book timed castle tickets, enjoy the beer gardens (Letná, Riegrovy) and go rafting in Krumlov. August is the busiest month.
strings.note2: Beer is 50-70 CZK (cheaper than water), goulash 200-250, svíčková 250, a croissant and coffee 100. Tip 10%. A cover charge is sometimes added to the bill.
strings.note3: Currency exchange offices often use a "0% commission" trick (bad rate). At ATMs, choose your own bank's rate. If you are offered payment in EUR, the rate is bad. You can pay by card everywhere.
strings.note4: The main castle circuit costs 450 CZK. Josefov is closed on Saturdays. Buy online tickets for the Sedlec Bone Church (no photography). Book the Krumlov bus (RegioJet) days ahead.
strings.note5: Trdelník is not Czech (it is Hungarian or Slovak) but it is tasty. Real Czech dishes: svíčková, vepřo knedlo zelo, smažený sýr (fried cheese), koláče (sweet pastries).
